I said it about twitter and I'll say it about Facebook, these are private (non-government funded) companies that can do whatever they want. If you get your news from FB you deserve what you get.

If it's something you care about, then the correct response to corporate censorship isn't to roll over and take it. If they get enough public backlash (which of course requires enough public awareness and lack of apathy) then they will be pressured to back off of these policies. When it's not a big deal for them, they'll keep doing it and keep moving the line of what's acceptable.

I link this a lot because I see a lot that people think you shouldn't complain about corporate censorship and that's really misguided imo. ACLU's 'what is censorship' page:

Private pressure groups, not the government, promulgated and enforced the infamous Hollywood blacklists during the McCarthy period. But these private censorship campaigns are best countered by groups and individuals speaking out and organizing in defense of the threatened expression.

While I understand what you are saying. I'm not rolling over and taking it, I'm choosing not to support a site that behaves in this manner. Corporations lose their power when people stop supporting them. Facebook or any company is allowed to delete or steer a narrative however they want and it's also my choice not to support them. Unless you have the energy to try to point out every single instance of censorship it's better to just go somewhere else.

With the understanding that neither approach (that is, actively protesting vs. quietly going elsewhere) is likely to succeed or have much of an impact without achieving some kind of critical mass, would you at least agree that attempts by the public to hold them accountable is a valid response to that sort of thing and it doesn't change just because they aren't the government? For instance, if people don't know what's going on, they might not even bother to go elsewhere.

We're both not discussing this on reddit and I personally don't have a facebook account so I think we both agree with the concept of not supporting those organizations whose policies don't sit right with us, but I wouldn't hold it against anyone that wants to fight from within or otherwise campaign for free speech on these platforms.

By all means shout it from the rooftops if it helps, the more people that know a source is biased the better. However, don't act like these companies owe the public free and uncensored speech because they do not.
This is what we have to keep doing. Keep fighting the good fight against censorship, keep the pressure up on these companies.
